results.corrected_title: TSMC posts record Q3 profit and guides higher, but shares slip on margin worries
results.corrected_summary: On 15 October 2026 TSMC reported Q3 2026 revenue of NT$1,494.24bn (US$46.72bn) and net income of NT$763.06bn. Net income rose 68.7% year on year. Gross margin was 66.4%, down from 67.7% in Q2; the company largely blamed the early ramp of its 2nm process. It guided Q4 revenue to US$52.3–54.3bn with a 65–67% gross margin, and the shares fell after the report on worries about margin dilution and capital spending.
key_facts: Q3 2026 revenue NT$1,494.24bn (US$46.72bn); net income NT$763.06bn, up 68.7% y/y; diluted EPS NT$29.43
2nm made up 8% of Q3 wafer revenue; CFO Wendell Huang pointed to a 'steep ramp-up' of 2nm in Q4
Q4 2026 guidance: revenue US$52.3–54.3bn, gross margin 65–67%
Shares fell after the results despite the earnings beat
results.issues: The CNBC URL returned 403 and could not be opened. The figures were confirmed from the TSMC filing on the SEC site. The share drop and the 1.3pp quarter-on-quarter margin fall (67.7% to 66.4%) come from search-result summaries; the size of the share drop was not confirmed. Year-on-year revenue growth differs by currency (50.9% in NT$, about 41% in US$), so the summary leaves it out.

results.corrected_title: ASML posts record Q3 sales; some customers want to order machines for 2029–2030
results.corrected_summary: On 14 October 2026 ASML reported record Q3 net sales of €11.7bn, net income of €5.0bn and a 57.5% gross margin. It sold 121 lithography systems, 17 of them EUV. It guided Q4 sales to €14.2–15.2bn and raised its full-year 2026 forecast to €44–45bn. CEO Christophe Fouquet said some customers want to place orders for 2029 and even 2030, that supply planned for 2027–2028 will not fully meet demand, and that ASML is looking at adding capacity beyond the 30% increase it had already announced.
key_facts: Q3 2026 net sales €11.7bn (record), net income €5.0bn, gross margin 57.5%
121 systems sold (113 new, 8 used), 17 of them EUV
Q4 guidance €14.2–15.2bn; FY2026 raised to €44–45bn with a gross margin of about 56%
Fouquet: some customers want to place orders for 2029 and even 2030; this is interest, not firm orders
Supply planned for 2027–2028 will not fully meet demand; ASML is looking at capacity beyond the earlier 30% increase

best_source.name: The Globe and Mail (ASML press release)

results.issues: Quartz and CNBC returned 403. The 121-system count and the Fouquet quotes come from search-result summaries of several outlets. The page summary of the Globe and Mail text oddly named the CEO 'Andrew Saunders', which is almost certainly an extraction error; search results confirm Christophe Fouquet made the remarks. The 2029–2030 orders are expressions of interest, not booked orders, and ASML no longer publishes bookings.

results.corrected_title: Samsung and SK hynix plunge after China's CXMT claims a DRAM breakthrough; Kospi hit by circuit breaker two days later
results.corrected_summary: At a chip conference in Shanghai on 9–10 October 2026, CXMT CEO Cao Kanyu said a server DRAM chip using a 4F² cell design should launch before year-end. On 13 October Samsung Electronics fell 7.39% to 232,000 won, SK hynix fell 10.09% to 1,443,000 won, and the Kospi closed down 5.46% at 6,035.35, triggering a sell-side sidecar. On 15 October the Kospi fell another 7.57% to 5,554.22 after hotter-than-expected US September inflation data and doubts about AI spending, and a circuit breaker halted trading for 20 minutes.
key_facts: CXMT CEO Cao Kanyu made the 4F² claim at a chip conference in Shanghai on 9–10 October; CXMT has not disclosed yields, speeds or volumes
13 Oct: Samsung -7.39% (232,000 won), SK hynix -10.09% (1,443,000 won), Kospi -5.46% to 6,035.35 with a sell-side sidecar
15 Oct: Kospi -7.57% to 5,554.22, a six-month low; circuit breaker at 12:38 p.m. halted trading for 20 minutes
US September inflation came in at 3.7% against a 3.6% forecast, adding to the sell-off
4F² can cut DRAM cell area by about a third versus today's 6F²; Samsung is reportedly targeting 4F² mass production around 2028
results.issues: The candidate dated the CXMT claim to 10 October only; the conference ran 9–10 October and no single date was confirmed. The Kospi figures for 13 October (-5.46%, 6,035.35) and the 15 October close (-7.57%) and inflation numbers come from search-result summaries. The Korea Herald article was published intraday (Kospi -8.13% at 1:17 p.m.) and does not mention inflation. The 15 October fall had several causes beyond CXMT (US inflation, AI doubts), so it is presented as a follow-on sell-off, not purely a reaction to CXMT. Confidence is medium because some details rest on search summaries.
